questions.prompt: A boat moves east at \(4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) relative to water. The river flows north at \(3\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find boat velocity relative to ground.
Using \(\vec{v}_{BG}=4\hat{\imath}+3\hat{\jmath}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), find ground speed.
If \(\vec{v}_{AB}=7\hat{\imath}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), what is \(\vec{v}_{BA}\)?
A person walks forward at \(1.2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) on a train moving forward at \(15\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find person velocity relative to ground.
A person walks backward at \(1.2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) on a train moving forward at \(15\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find person velocity relative to ground.
questions.answer:
\[
v_{PG}=-1.2+15=13.8\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}
\]
The result is still forward relative to the ground.

questions.prompt: A boat aims due north at \(6\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) relative to water. The current is east at \(2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find drift angle east of north.
questions.answer:
\[
\tan\theta=\frac{2}{6}
\]
\[
\theta=18.4^\circ
\]

questions.prompt: A plane has airspeed \(80\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) east. Wind is \(20\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) west. Find ground velocity.
questions.answer:
\[
v_{PG}=80-20=60\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}
\]
The direction is east.

questions.prompt: A plane has airspeed \(80\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) east. Wind is \(20\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) north. Find ground speed.
A drone moves \(5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) north relative to air. Wind is \(2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) south. Find ground velocity.
questions.answer:
\[
v_{DG}=5-2=3\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}
\]
The direction is north.

questions.prompt: A plane wants a ground velocity due east at \(100\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Wind is north at \(20\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). What must the plane's air-velocity components be?
questions.answer:
The north wind must be cancelled by a southward air component:
\[
\vec{v}_{PA}=100\hat{\imath}-20\hat{\jmath}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}
\]

questions.prompt: If \(\vec{v}_{PA}=\vec{v}_{PB}+\vec{v}_{BA}\), solve for \(\vec{v}_{PB}\).
A swimmer can swim \(2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) north relative to water. Current is \(1\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) east. Find swimmer velocity relative to ground.
A walkway moves east at \(1\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). A person walks west at \(1.5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) relative to the walkway. Find ground velocity, east positive.
questions.answer:
\[
v_{PG}=-1.5+1=-0.5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}
\]
The person moves west relative to the ground.

questions.prompt: A rain drop falls vertically at \(8\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) relative to air. Wind blows east at \(6\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find rain velocity relative to ground.

A boat has speed \(4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) relative to water. Current is \(3\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) east. Find all possible ground-speed magnitudes and the headings that produce minimum and maximum values.
questions.answer:
Let \(|\vec v_{BW}|=4\) and \(|\vec v_{WG}|=3\) east.
Ground speed is \(|\vec v_{BG}|=|\vec v_{BW}+\vec v_{WG}|\).
By vector bounds,
\[
||4-3||\le |\vec v_{BG}|\le 4+3
\]
\[
1\le v_{BG}\le 7\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}
\]
Maximum \(7\) occurs when boat aims east (with current), minimum \(1\) when aiming west (against current).

questions.prompt: Car A moves east at \(25\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Car B moves north at \(15\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find \(\vec v_{AB}\), its magnitude, and its direction measured from east toward north.
questions.answer:
\[
\vec v_{AG}=25\hat\imath,
\quad
\vec v_{BG}=15\hat\jmath
\]
\[
\vec v_{AB}=\vec v_{AG}-\vec v_{BG}=25\hat\imath-15\hat\jmath
\]
\[
|\vec v_{AB}|=\sqrt{25^2+15^2}=29.2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}
\]
Direction from east toward north is negative (toward south):
\[
	heta=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{-15}{25}\right)=-31.0^\circ
\]
So A moves \(31.0^\circ\) south of east relative to B.

questions.prompt: Why must relative velocities be added as vectors?
questions.answer: Directions matter. Crossed motions, such as east and north components, cannot be combined by ordinary scalar addition.

questions.prompt: A pilot wants a ground track due north at \(120\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Wind is \(35\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) east. Find required heading angle and required airspeed.
questions.answer:
Need
\[
\vec v_{PG}=\vec v_{PA}+\vec v_{AG}=120\hat\jmath
\]
with wind \(\vec v_{AG}=35\hat\imath\).
Hence
\[
\vec v_{PA}=-35\hat\imath+120\hat\jmath
\]
Required airspeed:
\[
|\vec v_{PA}|=\sqrt{35^2+120^2}=125\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}
\]
Heading angle west of north:
\[
	an\theta=\frac{35}{120}\Rightarrow \theta=16.3^\circ
\]

questions.prompt: If frame B moves with constant velocity relative to A, derive the relation between \(\vec a_{PA}\) and \(\vec a_{PB}\). Then state what changes if B has constant nonzero acceleration relative to A.
questions.answer:
Start with
\[
\vec r_{PA}=\vec r_{PB}+\vec r_{BA}
\]
Differentiate twice:
\[
\vec a_{PA}=\vec a_{PB}+\vec a_{BA}
\]
If B has constant velocity relative to A, \(\vec a_{BA}=0\), so
\[
\vec a_{PA}=\vec a_{PB}
\]
If B has constant nonzero acceleration, then
\[
\vec a_{PA}=\vec a_{PB}+\vec a_{BA}
\]
so accelerations differ by that frame acceleration.

questions.prompt: For \(\vec r_{PA}=6\hat\imath+2\hat\jmath\,\mathrm m\), \(\vec r_{BA}=4\hat\imath-\hat\jmath\,\mathrm m\), and \(\vec v_{BA}=(-2\hat\imath+3\hat\jmath)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), find \(\vec r_{PB}\) and \(\vec v_{PB}\) given \(\vec v_{PA}=5\hat\imath+\hat\jmath\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).
questions.answer:
Position relation:
\[
\vec r_{PA}=\vec r_{PB}+\vec r_{BA}
\Rightarrow
\vec r_{PB}=\vec r_{PA}-\vec r_{BA}
\]
\[
\vec r_{PB}=(6\hat\imath+2\hat\jmath)-(4\hat\imath-\hat\jmath)
=2\hat\imath+3\hat\jmath\,\mathrm m
\]
Velocity relation:
\[
\vec v_{PA}=\vec v_{PB}+\vec v_{BA}
\Rightarrow
\vec v_{PB}=\vec v_{PA}-\vec v_{BA}
\]
\[
\vec v_{PB}=(5\hat\imath+\hat\jmath)-(-2\hat\imath+3\hat\jmath)
=7\hat\imath-2\hat\jmath\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}
\]

questions.prompt: A swimmer speed relative to water is \(2.5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). River current is \(1.0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) east, river width \(120\,\mathrm m\). Compare (i) minimum-time crossing and (ii) zero-drift crossing: find heading, crossing time, and downstream drift in each strategy.
questions.answer:
Given \(v_{SW}=2.5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), current \(v_{WG}=1.0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) east, width \(L=120\,\mathrm m\).

(i) Minimum-time crossing: maximize north component, so aim due north.
\[
v_{north}=2.5,
\quad
t_{\min}=\frac{120}{2.5}=48.0\,\mathrm s
\]
Downstream drift:
\[
d=1.0(48.0)=48.0\,\mathrm m\ \text{east}
\]

(ii) Zero-drift crossing: require west component to cancel current.
\[
2.5\sin\theta=1.0\Rightarrow \theta=23.6^\circ\ \text{west of north}
\]
North component then
\[
v_{north}=2.5\cos\theta=2.29\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}
\]
\[
t=\frac{120}{2.29}=52.4\,\mathrm s,
\quad d=0
\]
Tradeoff: minimum-time is faster but drifts; zero-drift is slower but lands directly opposite.

questions.prompt: An aircraft has fixed airspeed \(200\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Wind is \(60\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) from west to east. The aircraft flies out-and-back along an east-west line over equal ground distances. Derive total travel time and average ground speed for the round trip, and compare to no-wind case.
questions.answer:
Let aircraft airspeed be \(u=200\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), wind \(w=60\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) east.
Ground speeds along route:
\[
v_{\text{out}}=u+w=260,
\qquad
v_{\text{back}}=u-w=140\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}
\]
For one-way ground distance \(D\):
\[
t_{\text{tot}}=\frac{D}{260}+\frac{D}{140}
=D\left(\frac{1}{260}+\frac{1}{140}\right)
=\frac{2Du}{u^2-w^2}
\]
Numerically:
\[
t_{\text{tot}}=0.01099\,D\ \text{s (if \(D\) in m)}
\]
Round-trip average ground speed:
\[
\bar v=\frac{2D}{t_{\text{tot}}}=\frac{u^2-w^2}{u}=\frac{200^2-60^2}{200}=182\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}
\]
No-wind round-trip average would be \(200\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), so wind lowers average by \(18\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) despite helping one leg.
